about: Word/RichEdit visibility of every cmap code point of every installed non-Ex Shree font family (one representative face each). Word = Microsoft Word 16.0.18429 (free edition) via COM: the test .docx opened read-only, exported to PDF (ExportAsFixedFormat) and each line read from the PDF content stream (font, code, embedded glyph outline) and from the PDF rendered by Windows.Data.Pdf at 225 dpi (ink compared, 1px-tolerant F1, with the glyph drawn by GDI ExtTextOut ETO_GLYPH_INDEX at 75 px/em); also Word's own picture of each line (Range.EnhMetaFileBits, EMR_EXTTEXTOUTW records). RichEdit = msftedit.dll RICHEDIT50W in a hidden window: typed (WM_CHAR after EM_SETCHARFORMAT to the face) and pasted RTF (the product's RichTextClipboard.BuildRtf bytes via EM_SETTEXTEX ST_SELECTION), then EM_GETCHARFORMAT per character and EM_FORMATRANGE ink.

measured.thisSession: 2026-10-18 09:40-10:20: (a) the first session tested every mapped code point, every table-written unmapped one and the cp1252 punctuation, but not the ASCII 0x20-0x7E code points missing from a cmap - those 41 lines (24 families) were written as fam/xa-<family>.docx, exported by Word (one NEW hidden instance per document, opened read-only, PDF + Range.EnhMetaFileBits per paragraph; exportall.log/emfall.log 09:45-09:54; every instance quit, no WINWORD left) and run through RichEdit typed + RTF; (b) step 1 re-verified with an independent reader (verify-cmap.js -> verify-cmap.txt: 143 faces, 0 gid mismatches, 0 shared glyph ids, identical-outline sets equal); (c) 'draws' re-resolved for ASCII, punctuation and failing code points (finalize.js; draws-changes.txt; drawsOld keeps the first session's text) with the Bangla family-differing codes checked by rendering (bangla-check*.png, check4.png) and 198 glyphs with no table pair/composer truth looked at by eye (eye-0/50/100/150.png); (d) extra-ban/extra-guj7 Word results re-analysed (extra-word-check.json); (e) asInput: what the wired forward tables write for every ASCII/punctuation input character (final-input.txt).

findings: STEP 1. Every face of every family has the same (3,1) cmap (first session; re-checked this session by a second, independent TTF reader: 143 faces, 0 gid mismatches). No two code points share a glyph id in any font. Identical outlines (sameOutlineAs in fam/<family>.json): U+00B7=U+2219 in every family; SHREE-ASS/BAN U+0009=U+0192; ASS7/BAN7/Ass7-00x/Ban7-00x U+00A8=U+0192; Ass7-00x/Ban7-00x U+002D=U+00AD; DEV U+00B4=U+2014, U+0219=U+021A=U+021B=U+021C; DEV7/Dev7-00x U+005C=U+2019 U+005F=U+2018 U+0060=U+00B6 U+00B3=U+0160 U+00B4=U+2014 (Dev7-00x also U+00AB=U+0152); GUJ7/Guj7-00x U+005C=U+2019 U+005F=U+201C U+0060=U+2018 U+00B4=U+00B6 U+00F7=U+201D; KAN/KAN7 U+005C=U+2122 U+005F=U+0161 U+00B4=U+00B6 U+00F7=U+0152 U+2018=U+2019 (Kan7-00x without the last); MAL7/Mal7-00x U+0026=U+00AD U+005C=U+00DE U+005F=U+00ED U+0060=U+00DD U+00B4=U+00EE; TAM/TAM7/Tam7-00x U+0023=U+00B4 U+0026=U+00AD U+0040=U+00F7 U+005C=U+0152 U+005F=U+201D U+0060=U+2039; TEL/TEL7/Tel7-00x U+007B=U+201C U+00B6=U+00E6.

C1 code points U+0081 U+008D U+008F U+0090 U+009D U+009E: Word keeps the Shree font and the code (EMF) but GDI draws NO ink (ExtTextOutW by character: 0 px; the same glyph by index: 27-682 px; re-run this session with wordvis gdichar for GUJ7, Guj7-001, DEV7, SHREE-BAN: char ink 0 for every C1 code, U+0041 441 px both ways), so Word shows an empty advance; Word's PDF export writes them as WinAnsi codes, so PDF viewers draw the bullet glyph (81 8D 8F 90 9D) or .notdef (9E); RichEdit typed and RTF keep the advance and draw nothing. No other code point reaches these glyphs. Tables writing them: GUJ (guj7 and guj456) U+0081 for EVERY en dash (U+2013 -> U+0081) and em dash (U+2014 -> U+0081 U+0081), U+008D for ÷, U+008F for ૰; DEV (dev7 and dev456) U+008D for every en/em dash (U+2013 -> U+008D, U+2014 -> U+008D U+008D), U+0081 ×, U+008F ÷, U+0090 a blank glyph (5 pairs); main ban7 U+0081 ব্ঢ, U+008D ব্ড, U+0090 চ্ঞ (13 pairs each; U+008D is not even in the SHREE-ASS/ASS7/Ass7-00x cmaps); worktree ban7/ban456 also U+009E ৱ; ass7/ass456/ass7w U+0081 U+0090; ori7 U+008F ୰, U+0090 ଽ.

RichEdit (typed and RTF alike) sets charset 238 on U+0120-U+012F U+0152 U+0153 U+0160 U+0161 U+0178 U+0192; GDI then binds Arial and the Latin letter is drawn (U+0161 -> š). Word draws all of them. Heaviest table use: main ban7 U+0161 (প) 886 pairs, U+0192 (দ) 848; tel7 U+0153 868, U+0192 504, U+0160 448, U+0178 396, U+0152 32; kan7 U+0161 54, U+0178 41, U+0153 35. \fcharset0 in the RTF font table changes nothing; \fcharset2 turns them into C1 bytes and hides them (rtf-variants.json). The product's RTF (\fnil, \uN?) opened by Word gives the same result as the .docx for 658/658 lines (SHREE-GUJ7, SHREE-BAN7, SHREE-TEL7).
RichEdit moves U+2219 to Cambria Math; no table writes U+2219 and U+00B7 has the identical outline and is drawn by everyone.

U+00AD: a blank glyph in most families; Word on screen (EMF) draws it as the font does, Word's PDF draws the font's '-' glyph (WinAnsi AD = hyphen). Where U+00AD has ink (TAM, TAM7, Tam7-00x, MAL7, Mal7-00x: a minus; Ass7-00x, Ban7-00x: '-') Word draws it and RichEdit hides it (0 advance). Not in the KAN/KAN7/Kan7-00x/SAN7 cmaps: Word uses Cambria, RichEdit hides it. No table writes U+00AD.

NEW (this session): ASCII missing from the cmap - U+003C '<' in 21 of the 24 requested families (only SHREE-TEL, SHREE-TEL7 (draws ్ఱ) and SHREE-PUN7 (draws ₹) map it; of the extra families Kan7-00x and Mal7-00x lack it, Ori7-00x draws ₹, Tam7-00x a blank, Tel7-00x ్ఱ), SHREE-ASS7 also '%' and ':', SHREE-MAL7/Mal7-00x also '>' 'F' 'G' 'H' '[' '{', SHREE-PUN/PUN7 also 'x' '{'. Word draws the real character in Cambria (PDF and EMF). RichEdit (typed and RTF) draws the font's .notdef box, except in SHREE-BAN and SHREE-ASS where it draws ॥ (these fonts have usFirstCharIndex 0x20, so GDI's default character is 0x1F, which they map to ॥); the same ॥ appears for U+201B there. No table pair writes these, but FontConverter copies an input character with no pair through unchanged, so a '<' in Unicode input reaches the legacy run.

NEW: input characters that the converter copies through and the font draws as NOTHING (in every program, font-level): DEV/DEV7/Dev7-00x and GUJ/GUJ7/Guj7-00x '$' and '>'; SAN7 '>'; KAN/KAN7/Kan7-00x '$'; MAL7/Mal7-00x '-' (hyphen!); TAM/TAM7 '-' and Tam7-00x '-' '<'; ORI/ORI7/Ori7-00x '&'; Shree-Ban7-00x '%' and ':'; U+00A0 everywhere (blank by design). Punctuation pairs that write a code whose glyph is something else: kan7 U+2014 -> U+2014 (draws ಽ), U+2018 -> U+2018 (ೞ); tel7 U+2013 (ృ), U+2014 (ఁ), U+2018 (।), U+2019 (an asterisk-like sign); tam7 U+2013 (×); ori7 U+201D -> U+201D (ଦ୍ଦ); main ban7 U+2013 -> U+2013 (ঃ in BAN7/ASS7/Ban7-00x, the half-ন hook in BAN/ASS/Ass7-00x) and U+2014 -> U+2014 (spacing ৺-like sign in the 7 fonts, zero-width subscript ্ন in the 4/5/6 fonts); the worktree Bangla tables write U+2013/U+2014 as hyphens instead. Full list: final-input.txt.

NEW: the first session's names for the Bangla family-differing codes were wrong in places (it took the 7 composer's meaning, which follows the 4/5/6 layout there). Rendered check (bangla-check.png) and fontCheck agree: '@' = ঃ in SHREE-BAN, SHREE-ASS, Shree-Ass7-00x but the half-ন hook in SHREE-BAN7, SHREE-ASS7, Shree-Ban7-00x; U+2013 = the hook in BAN/ASS/Ass7-00x but ঃ in the 7 group; U+2014 = zero-width subscript ্ন in BAN/ASS/Ass7-00x but a spacing ৺-like sign in the 7 group; '%' = a zero-width below mark in SHREE-BAN7 (not in the ASS7 cmap, blank in Ban7-00x); U+0152 = ধ্ম in BAN/ASS but a copy of ব in BAN7/ASS7/Ban7-00x/Ass7-00x. Also SHREE-SAN7 'n' (U+006E) is the zero-width subscript ्न (the San composer writes ” as 6E, a quirk). Main's languages.json wires SHREE-BAN-xxxx (4/5/6) to shree-ban7, so these codes come out swapped there.

U+00A0 is written by Word as U+0020 (both blank in every font). U+017E and U+017D fall back to Cambria and U+20AC to Times New Roman in Word (re-analysed this session: extra-word-check.json); no shipped table writes them.
SHREE-DEV U+0219-U+021C have malformed glyf entries (bbox 20000,20000,-20000,-20000): nothing is drawn by anyone; no table writes them.

Name collision: SHREE-ORI7-0603/0604 are both S0603892/S0604892.TTF and WORI7001/7002.TTF; GDI binds the name to WORI7001.TTF (53,248 bytes, head checksumAdjustment 05AFB4F1), whose cmap adds U+003C (₹).

Glyph names: composer truth (single-byte answers of S8<Scr>764) only for GUJ, DEV, SAN, BAN/ASS; ORI, PUN, TAM, TEL, KAN, MAL names come from the shipped reverse tables, the forward tables (pieces) or the eye check only.
